question.problem:
$$
A=[\begin{aligned}2 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & 2 \\ 0 & 2 & -2\end{aligned}],\,D=[\begin{aligned}2 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 2 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & -3\end{aligned}]
$$

Consider the matrices shown above. 
Given that $D={P}^{T}\,AP,$ where $P$ is an orthogonal matrix, which of the following could be the first and second columns of the matrix $P?$
question.worked_solution:
Recall that a matrix $A$ is orthogonally diagonalizable if there exists an orthogonal matrix $P$ such that

$$
A=PD{P}^{T},
$$

where $D$ is a diagonal matrix. Equivalently,

$$
D={P}^{T}AP.
$$

Moreover, a matrix $A$ is orthogonally diagonalizable if and only if it is symmetric.

First, note that $A$ is symmetric and $D$ is diagonal. Therefore, $D={P}^{T}\,AP$ gives an orthogonal diagonalization of $A.$

From the diagonal matrix $D$ we deduce that the eigenvalues of the matrix $A$ are ${\lambda }_{1}=2,$ ${\lambda }_{2}=2,$ and ${\lambda }_{3}=-3.$ So, the first and second columns of $P$ correspond to the eigenvalues ${\lambda }_{1}$ and ${\lambda }_{2}.$ 

Now, we need to find  eigenvectors that correspond to ${\lambda }_{1}={\lambda }_{2}=2.$ Computing $A-2I,$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}A-2I & =[\begin{aligned}2 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & 2 \\ 0 & 2 & -2\end{aligned}]-2[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}0 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & -1 & 2 \\ 0 & 2 & -4\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

Seeking a non-zero solution of $(A-2I)x=0$ gives two eigenvectors: 

$\,$ ${v}_{1}=[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 0 \\ 0\end{aligned}]\,$ and $\,{v}_{2}=[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 2 \\ 1\end{aligned}]$

Notice that eigenvectors ${v}_{1}$ and ${v}_{2}$ are  orthogonal. So, we divide ${v}_{1}$ and ${v}_{2}$ by their respective norms, to obtain the first and second columns of $P:$  

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{{v}_{1}}{‖{v}_{1}‖} & =[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 0 \\ 0\end{aligned}] \\ \frac{{v}_{2}}{‖{v}_{2}‖} & =\frac{1}{\sqrt{5}}[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 2 \\ 1\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}0 \\ \frac{2\sqrt{5}}{5} \\ \frac{\sqrt{5}}{5}\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$
